text:
B: Hello! Oh, hiya, is it Kasia?
A: Yes, hello. And you're Nicola?
B: I am. Lovely to meet you. Third call, I'm getting the hang of it now. Where are you based?
A: Warrington. Originally Poland, but I've been in Warrington years now.
B: Oh, lovely. I'm up in Lancaster. Whereabouts in Poland, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Opole. It's in the south-west. Not so famous, most people haven't heard of it.
B: I haven't, I'm afraid, but I've always wanted to go to Kraków. All that architecture. I've got a list in a notebook of places I'm going to go when things pick up, and Kraków's on it.
A: Kraków is beautiful, yes. Very busy in summer, though. Go in October.
B: October, noted. What do you do?
A: I'm a biomedical scientist, in a hospital lab. Haematology.
B: Ooh, that sounds very clever. I could never do anything like that, I was useless at science. I'm more of an art person. I'm doing an art history degree with the Open University, and before that I was a picture framer for years.
A: It's not so clever. It's mostly careful. You check things twice and then you check again.
B: Well, that's what framing was like, really. Measure twice, cut once. A mitre that's a millimetre out and the whole thing looks wrong. Do you have much time for art and that, with shifts?
A: Not really, honestly. I'm not a big gallery person. I read crime novels and watch box sets. But I went to the Walker in Liverpool once and I liked it more than I expected.
B: Oh, the Walker's wonderful! What did you see?
A: Erm, I don't remember the names. There was a big painting with a boy being asked questions by soldiers, everybody standing around him. I stood there a long time.
B: "And When Did You Last See Your Father?" That's the one. Isn't it gorgeous? The little sister crying in the back. I've written about narrative painting for one of my essays, actually, and I always think that's the perfect example, the whole story's in the boy's face. Sorry, I'm getting carried away.
A: No, it's interesting. I didn't know the name. Now I know.
B: You've got a good eye, though, picking that one out.
A: Maybe. Or it was just big.
B: Ha! Well, that's honest. Do you have anything on your walls at home?
A: A wedding photo. And a calendar from the Polish shop. That's my collection.
B: That's a perfectly good collection. I was talking to Kirsty earlier, she does these drawings of canal locks. You should see them.
A: Oh, I spoke to her too. She has the cat who throws pencils.
B: The very same. Everyone's got a cat knocking things off windowsills today.
A: Mine is the worst, I think. Last week the basil.
B: Oh no, not the basil. Mine's my mum's phone. Every week she rings me, "Nicola, it's gone funny again"—
A: Oh, sorry, I think it's finishing.
